title: Reanimate a LEGO Mindstorms NXT Robot with AI

questions.q: Why must an NXT motor be driven through an H-bridge rather than directly from a GPIO pin?
choices: Because GPIO pins only output 5 V, which is too much for the motor
Because the motor can draw up to about 1 A and produces an inductive kickback spike, both of which would destroy a 3.3 V GPIO pin
Because the H-bridge converts the Pi's digital signal into the analog pulses a hobby servo needs
Because gpiozero refuses to talk to a motor unless an H-bridge is present
questions.explain: A GPIO pin can safely supply only about 16 mA, but an NXT motor draws tens of milliamps free-running and up to roughly 1 A when stalled. On top of that, switching the motor off makes its coil produce a sharp reverse-voltage spike (inductive kickback). The H-bridge handles the heavy current and its protection diodes absorb the spike, keeping the delicate GPIO pin safe.

questions.q: When wiring the DRV8833 motor driver, what is the correct power and ground arrangement?
choices: Power the motors from the Pi's 5 V pin and keep every ground separate
Use a separate ~9 V battery for the motors AND keep its negative completely isolated from the Pi
Use a separate ~9 V battery for the motors, but join its negative to the driver GND and the Pi GND as one common ground
Power both the Pi and the motors from the same 9 V battery
questions.explain: Motors get their own ~9 V battery (e.g. 6×AA) wired to the driver's VM input, because the Pi cannot supply that much current and motor noise can crash it. But the battery's negative, the driver GND and the Pi GND must all meet at one common ground, so the Pi's 3.3 V logic signals share a 0 V reference with the driver. Without a common ground, nothing works.

questions.q: The NXT motor contains a 'quadrature encoder'. What does that mean?
choices: A sensor with two channels offset by a quarter-step, so you can tell both how far AND which way the shaft turned
An encoder that only works when the motor spins at a quarter of full speed
A device that encrypts the motor's position data into four channels
A four-wire connector that carries the motor's power
questions.explain: A quadrature encoder watches a striped disc spin past two light sensors that are offset by a quarter of a step. By comparing which channel changes first, gpiozero's RotaryEncoder can work out both the distance turned and the direction. The NXT encoder gives roughly one count per degree (about 360 counts per revolution).

questions.q: The NXT encoder's tacho channels (and many NXT sensor lines) can sit near 5 V. What must you do before connecting them to a Pi GPIO input?
choices: Nothing — the Pi 5's GPIO pins are 5 V-tolerant
Put a single 330 Ω resistor in series to limit the current
Drop the voltage to a safe ~3.3 V or below using a voltage divider (level-shifting) before the GPIO pin
Connect them to a 5 V power pin instead of a GPIO pin
questions.explain: Pi 5 GPIO pins are 3.3 V logic and are NOT 5 V-tolerant; feeding them more than 3.3 V can permanently damage them. The encoder and sensor lines that exceed 3.3 V must pass through a voltage divider (for example 330 Ω then 470 Ω, giving about 2.94 V) so the GPIO only ever sees a safe level. A plain series resistor does not set the voltage; a divider does.

questions.q: In the camera-vision rover, the program follows a 'see → think → act' loop. Which sequence correctly describes it?
choices: Spin the motors, then read the encoder, then capture a frame
Capture a camera frame, run an object-detection model to find the target's position, then steer the motors to centre and approach it
Ask the user where the target is, then drive blindly towards it
Detect a bump, reverse, then take a photograph
questions.explain: The loop is: SEE — grab a frame with Picamera2; THINK — run an on-device object-detection model that returns boxes around recognised objects; ACT — use the target box's horizontal position to decide whether to turn left, turn right, or drive forward, then repeat. On a Pi 5 with TensorFlow Lite this runs at a few frames per second; the IMX500 AI Camera, which detects on-sensor, is much faster.
